A large language model is a program that writes text in reply to text that
you give it. LM Studio is a desktop app that downloads such models and runs
them on your own computer. The rlmstudio package lets you control LM Studio
from R. This vignette takes you from installing LM Studio to your first
replies from a model.

## Install LM Studio

LM Studio comes with a command-line tool called `lms`. The package uses
`lms` to start and stop parts of LM Studio. If you do not have LM Studio
yet, run `install_lmstudio(method = "browser")`. It opens the LM Studio
download page in your web browser. After you install LM Studio, restart R.

Load the package and check that R can find LM Studio.


``` r
library(rlmstudio)

# TRUE if R finds the lms tool
has_lms()
#> [1] TRUE

# TRUE if the lms tool is version 0.4.0 or later
check_lms_version()
#> ✔ LM Studio CLI is using the modern architecture (0.4.0+).
#> [1] TRUE
```

If either call returns `FALSE`, install or update LM Studio before you go
on.

## Start the server

R talks to LM Studio through a local server. A local server is a program
on your own computer that answers requests from other programs, such as R.
By default, the package sends its requests to `http://localhost:1234`.

`lms_server_start()` starts the server. The server needs a few seconds
before it answers, so the function waits for it. The `wait` argument sets
the most seconds that it waits. If the wait runs out, the function gives a
warning, and your script goes on. So call `lms_server_ready()` next. It
returns `TRUE` only when LM Studio answers.


``` r
# Start the server, and wait up to 30 seconds for it to answer
lms_server_start(wait = 30)
#> ✔ LM Studio server started successfully on the default port.

# TRUE if LM Studio answers
lms_server_ready()
#> [1] TRUE
```

## Find a model

A model key is the name that you give R to choose a model, such as
`"google/gemma-3-1b"`. `list_models()` shows the models that LM Studio
has on your computer, one row for each model. The `key` column holds the
model key.


``` r
# The models on this computer, one row each
list_models()
#>      state      type          display_name                                  key
#> 1 unloaded       llm           Gemma 4 E4B                   google/gemma-4-e4b
#> 2 unloaded       llm   Gemma 4 26B A4B QAT           google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-qat
#> 3 unloaded       llm         Qwen3 4B 2507                   qwen/qwen3-4b-2507
#> 4 unloaded       llm            Gemma 3 1B                    google/gemma-3-1b
#> 5 unloaded embedding Nomic Embed Text v1.5 text-embedding-nomic-embed-text-v1.5
#>   architecture size_gb
#> 1       gemma4    6.39
#> 2       gemma4   14.57
#> 3        qwen3    2.12
#> 4  gemma3_text    0.72
#> 5         <NA>    0.08
```

This vignette uses `google/gemma-3-1b`, a small model. Keep its key in a
variable, so that each call below can use it.


``` r
model <- "google/gemma-3-1b"
```

## Download the model

`lms_download()` asks LM Studio to download a model. For a model that is
already on your computer, it returns `"already_downloaded"`. For a new
model, it returns a job id. Pass the job id to `lms_download_status()` to
see the status of the download. Call `lms_download_status()` again until
the status says that the download finished.

When the output below was made, the model was already on the computer. So
the output shows the first case.


``` r
# Download the model, or find that it is already on disk
job_id <- lms_download(model)
#> ℹ Initiating download for model: "google/gemma-3-1b"...
#> ✔ Initiating download for model: "google/gemma-3-1b"... [847ms]
#> 
#> ✔ Model "google/gemma-3-1b" is already downloaded.
job_id
#> [1] "already_downloaded"

# The status of the download
lms_download_status(job_id)
#> 
#> ── Download Job: "N/A"
#> Status: already_downloaded
```

## Put the model in memory

Loading a model means that LM Studio reads it from disk into memory. A
model must be loaded before it can answer. `lms_load()` loads the model.


``` r
# Read the model into memory
lms_load(model)
#> ℹ Loading model: "google/gemma-3-1b"...
#> ✔ Model "google/gemma-3-1b" loaded and verified. [4.4s]
#> 
```

## Chat with the model

`lms_chat()` sends one prompt to the model and returns the reply as text.
The `input` argument holds your prompt.

A system prompt is a set of instructions that the model reads before your
prompt. Use it to set the role, the tone, or the length of the reply. The
`system_prompt` argument of `lms_chat()` holds it.


``` r
# Send one prompt, with a system prompt
reply <- lms_chat(
  model = model,
  input = "Say hello to a new R user.",
  system_prompt = "Answer in one short sentence."
)

# Print the text of the reply
cat(reply)
#> “Welcome aboard! It’s great to have you as a new R user!”
```

## Send several prompts in one call

A batch is a set of prompts that you send in one call, such as one prompt
for each row of your data. `lms_chat_batch()` sends each prompt in
`inputs` as its own request, with the same system prompt. It returns one
reply for each prompt, in the order of the prompts.


``` r
questions <- c(
  "Name a fruit.",
  "Name a color.",
  "Name a planet."
)

# One reply for each prompt, in the same order
answers <- lms_chat_batch(
  model = model,
  inputs = questions,
  system_prompt = "Answer with one word."
)
answers
#> [1] "Apple 🍎\n" "Blue \n"    "Mars \n"

# Remove the spaces and line breaks around each reply
trimws(answers)
#> [1] "Apple 🍎" "Blue"     "Mars"
```

`vignette("text-analysis")` shows how to get the replies of a batch as a
data frame, with one row for each prompt.

## Clean up

When you are done, unload the model to free its memory, and stop the
server.


``` r
# Remove the model from memory
lms_unload(model)
#> ℹ Unloading model: "google/gemma-3-1b"...
#> ✔ Model "google/gemma-3-1b" unloaded successfully. [413ms]
#> 

# Stop the local server
lms_server_stop()
#> ✔ LM Studio server stopped successfully.
```

## Without the desktop app

You can also run LM Studio on a computer that has no desktop app, such as
a remote server. `vignette("headless-config")` shows how to install and
use LM Studio that way.
